name: Gooseberry Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: 1 pint ripe or nearly ripe gooseberries
ingredients.originalText: 1 pint ripe or nearly ripe gooseberries
ingredients.quantityText: 1 pint ripe or nearly ripe gooseberries

instructions.text: Stew the gooseberries ten minutes—very slowly, not to break them
Cut your slices of bread to fit your pudding-dish, and toast to a light brown on both sides, cutting off all the crust before toasting
Dip each slice, while hot, in milk, and spread with the melted butter
Cover the bottom of the dish with them
Put next a layer of the gooseberries, sprinkled thickly with sugar
More toast, more berries, and so on, until the dish is full
Cover closely and steam in a moderate oven twenty or twenty-five minutes
Turn out upon a hot dish and pour over it a good pudding-sauce

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stew the gooseberries ten minutes—very slowly, not to break them
2. Cut your slices of bread to fit your pudding-dish, and toast to a light brown on both sides, cutting off all the crust before toasting
3. Dip each slice, while hot, in milk, and spread with the melted butter
4. Cover the bottom of the dish with them
5. Put next a layer of the gooseberries, sprinkled thickly with sugar
6. More toast, more berries, and so on, until the dish is full
7. Cover closely and steam in a moderate oven twenty or twenty-five minutes
8. Turn out upon a hot dish and pour over it a good pudding-sauce
